title: Font Attribute Ignored for Bold Numbers

illustrates.quote: Ignore font attributes for numbers/letters beginning exercise material, alphabetic divisions, etc.

blocks.features: Bold, green heading, title case (not full capitals — the braille's own single capital sign before each word, not the doubled sign used for a genuinely all-caps heading elsewhere in this section, e.g. example-5-7's 'SPELLING WORDS').
Three numbered questions in plain black text; only the numerals (1., 2., 3.) are bold.
items: **1.** Did your spider weave a web?
**2.** What time of day did your spider start to weave its web?
**3.** Did your spider build just one web?

print.notes: Illustrates ignoring the bold attribute on the numerals that begin each exercise item, per rule 5.3.9; the green heading's own decorative bold/colour is separately ignored per rule 5.3.1.
print.surroundingText: Follows rule 5.3.9 directly, on printed page 5-6, immediately after Example 5-8.
print.printFeatures: Bold green heading over a numbered question list with bold numerals, plain question text.

braille.notes: Six lines, margin 9 stripped. Line 1 is a full blank-cell filler line before the heading, kept as an empty string (same construct as Examples 5-4/5-7, both of which keep it). Line 2, the heading, sits at a fixed 4-cell indent — matching cell-5, not centered. Item 2 (lines 4-5) wraps to a 2-cell-indented runover. No bold indicator on the number signs ('#a4' etc.) or on the heading.

resolution: Braille re-derived independently from .txt lines 4001-4006 (margin 9); matches run A's 6-line rendering (including the leading blank line and item 2's genuine runover indent) exactly. Run B's 5-line, flush-stripped rendering is rejected for the same reasons as example-5-7/5-8 (documented section-wide indentation-stripping bug). Heading level (2, cell-5) newly measured against the fixed-4-cell convention. The heading's own wording was NOT taken from either run's prose account (both offered plausible-sounding but unverified captions) — decoded directly, letter by letter, from the braille itself using UEB's single-letter whole-word contractions (',:at'=What, ',y'=You, ',w'=Will, '4cov]'=Discover, each preceded by an ordinary single capital sign, not the doubled sign used for a genuinely all-caps heading elsewhere in this section) to 'What You Will Discover'.
